title: Precise synthesis of targeted noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A mixture of chloride or nitrate salts of several noble metals (e.g., Pt, Pd, Rh, Ir, Au, Ru) dissolved in a common solvent.
recollection.intervention: Guess: A wet-chemical co-reduction route, possibly using a strong reducing agent like NaBH4 or ethylene glycol under elevated temperature, with precise control of metal ratios and reaction kinetics.
recollection.structure: Guess: Sub-10 nm face-centered-cubic high-entropy alloy nanoparticles with uniform elemental distribution confirmed by STEM-EDS mapping.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Simultaneous nucleation followed by diffusion-mediated homogenization; kinetic control and ligand/solvent choice suppress element segregation and phase separation, allowing a single-phase random solid solution.
recollection.results: Guess: Achieved nanoparticles with entropy-stabilized single phase, average size ~5 nm, lattice parameter close to 3.9 Å; catalytic test (e.g., ORR or HER) showed mass activity 5–10 × higher than commercial Pt/C and stability retention >90 % after 10 000 cycles.

score.note: The recollection is largely incorrect. The paper used spray-drying followed by H2 thermal decomposition-reduction, producing porous 3D nanoframeworks rather than ~5 nm particles from wet-chemical co-reduction. Formation proceeded through preferential noble-metal reduction and H-mediated reduction/incorporation of other metals, not simultaneous nucleation. The stated dimensions, lattice parameter, catalytic reaction, activity enhancement, and cycling stability do not match the reported MOR results or phase-transition measurements.
